$comment: Curated fallback for the 54 elements Wikidata has NO P8000 electron-configuration claim for (confirmed genuinely absent 2026-07-18 via probe-configuration.ts: 64/118 truthy AND 64/118 any-rank — not a query bug). Format deliberately matches P8000: noble-gas core + spectroscopic notation, fed through the SAME electronsPerShell parser as the Wikidata claims. Genuine exceptions (Cu, Ag, Au, Pt, Ce, Gd, Pa, U, Np, Cm, Lr, ...) are written into the notation, so NO Aufbau/2n2 rule is ever applied — consistent with the spec's core decision. Language-agnostic (electrons per shell are numbers). Plain digits are fine; the parser normalizes both plain and unicode superscripts.
$verificationNote: $needsVerification lists the f-block (lanthanides Ce-Lu, actinides Ac-Lr) and the superheavies (Mt-Ts). The f-block carries several ground-state exceptions where references vary; the superheavies are theoretical PREDICTIONS, not measurements. Verify these against an authoritative source (e.g. NIST) before relying on them. The s/p/d entries (Ni-Br, Ag, Ir-At) are standard textbook values.
